extracted.intended_audience: exchange rule filers, fund sponsors, SEC staff, and market participants interested in listing/trading commodity-based trust shares (Spot Ether ETPs)
extracted.subtask_short: listing spot ether ETP on exchange
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluation criteria for a national securities exchange proposal to list and trade a Spot Ether exchange-traded product structured as Commodity-Based Trust Shares under BZX Rule 14.11(e)(4). Includes the legal tests, surveillance, custody, index, NAV, and disclosure requirements the Commission examines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 6(b)(5) — designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission must determine that the proposal is consistent with the requirements of section 6(b)(5) of the Act, specifically including: (i) the requirement that a national securities exchange's rules are designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Commodity-Based Trust Shares, this typically requires demonstrating the existence of a comprehensive surveillance-sharing agreement with a regulated market of significant size. The listing exchange must show that such arrangements would assist in detecting and deterring misconduct. The page discusses application of the test to CME Ether Futures and use of correlation analysis to show surveillance utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 6(b)(5) — designed to protect investors and the public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission must determine that the exchange proposal be designed, in general, to protect investors and the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange argues investor-protection benefits (e.g., reducing premium/discount volatility, lowering management fees via competition, reducing risks/costs relative to OTC or futures-only structures, providing a transparent regulated vehicle). The balance of investor protection concerns vs. manipulation concerns is a factor in approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulated market of significant size test
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'market of significant size' is a market (or group of markets) as to which: (a) there is a reasonable likelihood that a person attempting to manipulate the ETP would also have to trade on that market to manipulate the ETP, so that a surveillance-sharing agreement would assist the listing exchange in detecting and deterring misconduct; and (b) it is unlikely that trading in the ETP would be the predominant influence on prices in that market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrations include correlation analysis between spot and futures markets, measures of futures market liquidity and open interest, and relative scale of the ETP versus the underlying spot/futures markets. The page applies this test to CME Ether Futures, citing correlation data and volume metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive surveillance-sharing agreement — hallmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Surveillance-sharing agreements must provide for sharing of information about market trading activity, clearing activity, and customer identity; the parties should have reasonable ability to obtain access to and produce requested information; and no existing rules, laws, or practices would impede one party from obtaining/producing this information to the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint membership in the Intermarket Surveillance Group (ISG) has historically been treated as meeting this requirement. The document cites prior SEC statements emphasizing these hallmarks as necessary deterrents to manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other means to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission has recognized that the 'regulated market of significant size' standard is not the only means for satisfying section 6(b)(5); a listing exchange can demonstrate that 'other means to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices' are sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and arguments include market structure features (geographic diversity, fragmentation, arbitrage activity), index design resistant to manipulation, oversight procedures, custodian safeguards, and the practical difficulty/cost of manipulating fragmented global spot markets. The Exchange argues these 'other means' mitigate manipulation risk for ETH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manipulation of the ETP — correlation and detectability
rubrics_metrics.description: The record should show that fraud or manipulation that impacts prices in spot markets would likely similarly impact the related futures market, and that surveillance of that futures market can assist in detecting such impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing cites correlation measures (Sponsor's research: daily correlation 0.998 between spot ETH and CME Ether Futures over a sample period) and applies the same rationale as used in the Spot Bitcoin ETP Approval Order to justify that CME surveillance can capture spot-market effects relevant to an ETP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predominant influence on prices in spot and futures markets
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal should show it is unlikely that trading in the Shares would be the predominant influence on prices in the related regulated market (e.g., CME Ether Futures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment includes comparing projected Fund trading/holdings to total spot/futures market trading volume and liquidity. The Exchange notes large aggregate spot ETH 24-hour volume (e.g., averaged $9.4 billion) and argues the Fund would constitute a very small percentage of that, so it could not dominate prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index design and resistance to manipulation (IOSCO principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund values Shares based on an Index designed according to IOSCO Principals for Financial Indexes, aggregating executed trade flow across specified constituent ether spot trading platforms and employing methodology to reduce outlier impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index methodology specifics: observation window 3:00–4:00 p.m. ET; all 'Relevant Transactions' across constituent platforms are added, partitioned into 12 five-minute intervals; for each partition compute a volume-weighted median trade price; the Index is the equally-weighted average of those medians. The Index excludes futures prices. The Sponsor emphasizes design choices (partitioning, volume-weighted medians) to mitigate undue influence from outlying or large trades. Index Provider implements oversight through codified policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: NAV calculation and valuation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator will determine the Fund's NAV daily, as promptly as practical after 4:00 p.m. EST, valuing ether held based on the Index (or fair value if Index unavailable). NAV equals total assets (ether, cash, cash equivalents) less liabilities; NAV per Share is determined and disseminated daily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Index is not available or Sponsor decides it should not be used, holdings may be fair valued per Sponsor-approved policy. Any permanent change to NAV calculation methodology would require a proposed rule change under Rule 19b-4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and public disclosure of information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund's website must publicly and at no charge provide current NAV per Share, prior business day's NAV and reported closing price, the BZX Official Closing Price vs NAV and premium/discount calculation, and charts showing distribution of discounts/premiums for prior quarters, among other disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information must be accessible to market participants to enable assessment of price vs NAV and the frequency/distribution of premiums and discounts; the filing specifies content and cadence for dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custody, safekeeping, and private key controls for ether holdings
rubrics_metrics.description: Custodian policies, procedures, and controls for safekeeping, exclusive possession or control over the Fund's ether holdings, and protection against theft, loss, and unauthorized or accidental use of private keys should be consistent with industry best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Sponsor emphasizes that the Custodian is a NYDFS-chartered trust company, subject to extensive regulation and with a long track record. The filing references 'cold storage' as a safeguarding method and parallels the Commission's suggestions for broker-dealer controls for digital asset securities. Custodial arrangements are presented as mitigating custody-related concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation/redemption mechanics and authorized participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Creations and redemptions will occur in cash for Creation Baskets of 50,000 Shares; authorized participants use cash to buy/deliver ether on behalf of the Fund; Sponsor submits orders to purchase ether and the Cash Custodian handles cash movements and transactions with onboarded trading partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed operational steps are described for purchases and redemptions (cash in exchange for Shares, Sponsor orders to buy/sell ether, settlement through Cash Custodian and Transfer Agent). The mechanics affect liquidity, arbitrage, and potential for premiums/discounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund asset composition and staking policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund's assets will only consist of ether, cash, and cash equivalents. The Sponsor may, from time to time, stake a portion of the Fund's assets through trusted staking providers (which may include affiliates), and the Fund would receive staking rewards of ether tokens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staking activity and receipt of staking rewards are disclosed; staking has implications for liquidity, valuation, and treatment of staking rewards (may be treated as income to the Fund).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund legal/regulatory classification and applicable constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Per the Registration Statement, the Trust is neither an investment company registered under the 1940 Act nor a commodity pool for purposes of the CEA; neither the Trust, the Fund nor the Sponsor is subject to regulation as a commodity pool operator or a commodity trading adviser in connection with the Shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing clarifies which statutes/regimes apply (and do not apply) to the Fund, informing the scope of regulatory oversight and compliance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index provider governance and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The Index Provider (CF Benchmarks Ltd.) implements an oversight function and administers the Index through codified policies for Index integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing relies on public Index Provider documentation and emphasizes transparency and governance as factors reducing manipulation risk and supporting use of the Index for NAV valuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fallback valuation and rule-change requirement for permanent changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Index is not available or Sponsor decides not to use it, the Fund's holdings may be fair valued in accordance with Sponsor-approved policy; any permanent change to the calculation of the NAV would require a proposed rule change under Rule 19b-4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes procedural guardrails for valuation changes and signals that permanent methodological changes must go through the SEC rule-filing process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of precedent and court rulings in justification (Spot Bitcoin ETP Approval Order and Grayscale)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange relies on prior Commission orders (e.g., Spot Bitcoin ETP Approval Order) and D.C. Circuit decisions (Grayscale v. SEC) to justify that CME futures markets can constitute a regulated market of significant size and that correlation/surveillance arguments can satisfy section 6(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing cites how the Commission's prior reasoning (that CME surveillance can capture spot-market effects where correlation is high) and the court's remand require robust correlation/analysis; applicants should present comparable evidence and reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of market metrics to demonstrate significant size and market maturity
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide measurable metrics related to the futures market (trading volume, number of contracts traded, open interest, number of large open interest holders, unique accounts) to show market size and maturation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing supplies CME Ether Futures trading counts, open interest holder counts, and other statistics to demonstrate that the futures market has progressed and matured; such empirical evidence supports conclusions about detectability of manipulation and market significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surveillance-sharing via ISG membership as evidence of surveillance capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the Exchange and CME being members of the Intermarket Surveillance Group (ISG) can constitute a comprehensive surveillance-sharing agreement for purposes of Rule 14.11(e)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing notes that the Commission has historically held joint ISG membership to be sufficient and cites Wilshire Phoenix Disapproval and other precedent regarding ISG membership meeting surveillance-sharing hallmarks.
